testCase.expectations: One JEE Advanced paragraph-based physics set in English: one original experiment or setup (for example blocks on an incline joined over a pulley, then sliding onto a spring), stated once with every number the questions need, in SI units, and 3 single-answer multiple-choice questions with 4 options, one per skill (kinematics, Newton's laws, work and energy), each needing a different part of the setup. Every key follows from the stated numbers, the numbers agree across the questions (a speed one question computes is the speed the next one uses), and each wrong option comes from a real mistake (time to a mark instead of between marks, net force taken as friction, friction left out of an energy balance). Difficulty matches JEE Advanced's own paragraph questions, not a textbook's: each question needs several steps that combine at least two ideas (a result from one stage of the setup feeding the next, or two laws applied together), so no question is a single formula with numbers stated next to each other.
